pie: snígʷʰs h₂éǵroy ḱéyto. dʰugh₂térm̥ kapyónts ph₂tḗr ph₂wéni sédyet h₂éǵt-kʷe. dʰugh₂tḗr moy ǵʰiméni ǵeǵónh₁e. téwe méh₂tēr kʷsépi ḱémh₂t. h₁ń̥gʷney me ḱludʰí h₁yós nos péh₂si. nu méne dʰugh₂tréy ḱlutóm h₁nómn̥ dʰéh₁m̥. dʰúgh₂ter méne ḱóymoy h₂uksyéh₁s téwe-kʷe póteyey lewbʰéh₂ h₁syéh₁s h₂wĺ̥h₁neh₂ toy pl̥h₁éwih₂ h₁syéh₁t sríHgos te mē h₁pyéh₁t péh₂wr̥ te gʷʰr̥nuyéh₁t suHnéwes toy ǵeǵn̥h₁ih₁ént dʰugh₂téres-kʷe toy ǵeǵn̥h₁ih₁ént. nu mléwHt h₁n̥gʷnís-kʷe dʰégʷʰet.
english: Snow lay on the field. The father sat by the fire, grasping his daughter, and said: "A daughter is born to me in the winter. Your mother toiled in the night. Fire, hear me, you who guard us! Now I set a famous name for my daughter. Daughter, may you grow up in my household, and may you be dear to your husband; may there be much wool for you; may the frost not seize you; may the fire warm you; may sons be born to you, and may daughters be born to you." So he spoke, and the fire burned.

pie: ǵérh₂onts ḱéyto h₁ésyo-kʷe pnéwmn̥ h₁ím linékʷt. h₁ésyo ǵónh₁ōs h₁ím h₂m̥bʰí sth₂éh₁yont. wérh₁yet. ḱléwsete me. tr̥syóh₂ wódr̥ moy wéǵʰete. ph₂térn̥s h₁éymi. h₂éǵmn̥ ḱóm ph₂sté téwe-kʷe bʰréh₂term̥ mē stundté. ǵʰutóm moy médʰu h₁áyte dʰǵʰméh₁ me ḱélete h₂éḱmonm̥-kʷe stoh₂éyete. méne h₁nómn̥ memn̥té. nu h₂ew ne bʰéh₂t HrudHént-kʷe.
english: The old man lay, and his breath was leaving him. His offspring stood around him. He said: "Listen to me. I am thirsty; bring me water. I go to the fathers. Keep the flock together, and do not strike your brother. Give me libated mead, cover me with earth, and set up a stone. Remember my name." Then he did not speak again, and they cried out.

pie: pótis h₂éǵmn̥ h₂éǵrom ǵʰiméni h₂éǵet. snígʷʰs gʷémt h₂ew-kʷe ne gʷémt. h₁ésyo pótnih₂ sédyet stóygʰom-kʷe spéḱyet. wĺ̥kʷōs kʷsépi HrudHént. h₁ím h₂usési widét snígʷʰs h₁ésmi ḱéyto sríHgos h₁ím h₁épt mr̥twós h₁ést. h₁íh₂ h₁widʰéwh₂n̥s bʰúHt HréwdHt-kʷe. h₁ésyeh₂s póteys dayh₂wḗr h₁ludʰét. wérh₁yet. gʷénh₂ mē HréwdHs. téwe ǵónh₁om h₂élōh₂ téwe-kʷe h₂éǵrom péh₂soh₂. nu h₁widʰéwh₂ wérh₁t. h₁wésus h₁ési téwe-kʷe ḱóymoy tḱéyoh₂. h₁widʰéwh₂ h₁ésyo ḱóymoy tḱéyt.
english: In winter the husband drove the flock to the field. The snow came, and he did not come back. His wife sat by the fire and looked at the path. The wolves cried out in the night. At dawn she saw him; the snow lay on him; the frost seized him; he was dead. She became a widow and cried out. The brother of her husband came. He said: "Woman, do not cry out. I shall nourish your offspring, and I shall guard your field." Then the widow said: "You are good, and I shall dwell in your household." So the widow dwelt in his household.

pie: owis eḱwobʰyos eweket, "ḱerd angʰetai moi widontei ǵʰm̥onm̥ eḱwons aǵontm̥."
english: The sheep said to the horses: "My heart pains me, seeing a man driving horses."

pie: Hyudʰsmós légʰt h₁ésyo-kʷe suHnúbʰos sékʷt. Hyudʰsmós h₁ésm̥. h₁ógʷʰim gʷʰénm̥ h₃rēǵés-kʷe gʰóstins gʷʰénm̥. h₃rēǵés Hroth₂óm h₂éǵom. méǵh₂ moy ḱléwos h₁ésti. nu me mértis gʷm̥sḱéti ne-kʷe dedwóyh₂e. mórtōs m̥rént deywṓs ne m̥rént. h₁yód mórtosyo h₁nómn̥ gʷíh₃weti h₁ésyo ḱléwos ń̥dʰgʷʰitom h₁ésti. ḱléwos wos méǵh₂ h₁éstu. nu h₁ésyo pnéwmn̥ h₁ím linékʷt.
english: The warrior lay down and spoke to his sons: "I was a warrior. I slew the serpent, and I struck down the enemies of the king. I drove the chariot of the king. Great fame is mine. Now death is coming to me, and I am not afraid. Mortals die; the gods do not die. If the name of a man lives, his fame is imperishable. Let your fame be great." Then his breath left him.

pie: dʰugh₂tḗr h₁ésyeh₂s ph₂térm̥ gʷémt h₁ésyeh₂ey-kʷe h₂éǵt. h₂nḗr nos gʷegʷóme h₂isḱéti te. h₁ím yéh₂esi? dʰugh₂tḗr wérh₁t. yéh₂oh₂ gʰostéyōm-kʷe dʰéh₁mn̥ dedwóyh₂e. nu méh₂tēr h₁ésyeh₂ey mléwHt. mē tréses. h₁yód ḱóm ḱóymom h₁ludʰóm bʰéyh₂m̥. h₂nérm̥ dedórḱh₂e h₁wésus-kʷe h₁ésti. h₁ésyo dʰéh₁mn̥ ǵʰleynóm h₁ésti h₁ésyo-kʷe h₁éḱwōs HéHḱewes h₁ésmi. nu dʰugh₂tḗr stéh₂t h₁ésyeh₂s-kʷe méh₂term̥ gʷéh₂t.
english: The daughter came to her father, and he said to her: "A man has come to us; he seeks you. Will you go to him?" The daughter said: "I shall go, and I am afraid of the dwelling of strangers." Then the mother said to her: "Do not tremble! When I came to this household, I became afraid. I have seen the man, and he is good. His dwelling is bright; and his horses are swift." Then the daughter stood up and went to her mother.

pie: h₁widʰéwh₂ h₃réǵm̥ h₁ludʰét. h₃rḗǵnih₂ h₃rēǵi sédyet. h₁widʰéwh₂ bʰéh₂t. h₃réǵ h₁widʰéwh₂ h₁ésmi méne-kʷe pótis mr̥twós h₁ésti. méne póteys bʰréh₂teres méne h₂éǵrom kapyónti. méne me ǵónh₁om-kʷe h₂lékse. h₃rḗǵs h₁widʰéwh₂m̥ spéḱyet tóybʰos-kʷe mléwHt. kʷésmōy h₁éy h₁ésti? wéwkont. h₁éy nos h₁ésti. h₃rḗǵs h₂éǵt. h₁éy h₁widʰwéh₂s ǵónh₁ōy h₁ésti. h₁ím h₂ew dédh₃te h₁widʰwéh₂ey-kʷe déḱm̥t h₂ówins h₁opéyete. h₃réǵm̥ ḱluwént h₁ím-kʷe h₂ew dh₃ént.
english: The widow came before the king. The queen was sitting beside the king. The widow said: "King, I am a widow, and my husband is dead. The brothers of my husband are seizing my field. Protect me and my offspring!" The king looked at the widow, and said to them: "To whom does it belong?" They said: "It is ours." The king said: "It is for the offspring of the widow. Give it back, and give ten sheep to the widow." They heard the king, and gave it back.

pie: tóysōm ph₂tḗr mr̥twós h₁ést. tréyes bʰréh₂teres sdént. h₁éḱwons h₂éǵonts só bʰéh₂t. h₁éḱwōs moy h₁sénti. h₂érh₃yonts só wérh₁t. dwóh₁ moy h₁éḱwoh₁ dh₃dʰí. tóh₁ mē h₁opéyōh₂. nu bʰréh₂tēr h₂élyom stunédt h₂élyos-kʷe h₁ím stunédt. bʰugént déh₂nu-kʷe dr̥mént. déh₂nu h₁éḱwom h₂epó wéǵʰet. nu h₁ím wédni widónt bʰih₂ént-kʷe. h₂ówins ph₂sónts só HréwdHt. kʷíd dʰedʰh₁th₁és?
english: Their father was dead. The three brothers sat down. The one who drove the horses said: "The horses are mine." The one who ploughs said: "Give me two horses." "I shall not give them." Then one brother struck the other, and the other struck him. They fled, and they ran to the river. The river carried a horse away. Then they saw it in the water, and became afraid. The one who guards the sheep cried out: "What are you doing?"

pie: bʰréh₂teres mr̥twóm h₂usési dʰh₁méns h₁éǵʰs bʰéront. h₁ím pĺ̥h₂seh₂h₁ woséyont. h₂éǵmn̥ h₁ím sékʷeto. h₁ím dréwi logʰéyont péh₂wr̥-kʷe bʰoréyont. péh₂wr̥ h₁ím h₁éwset dʰuh₂mós-kʷe dyḗm úd h₁éyt. h₁ésyo pótnih₂ HréwdHt ḱwṓ-kʷe HréwdHt. nu h₁ím dʰǵʰméh₁ ḱélont. h₂éḱmonm̥ h₁ím upér stoh₂éyont mr̥twṓy-kʷe ǵʰutóm médʰu dh₃ént. sóh₂wl̥ séngʷt. nu kʷséps gʷémt ḱwṓ-kʷe h₂ḱméni légʰt.
english: At dawn the brothers carried the dead man out of the dwelling. They clothed him in a garment. The procession followed him. They laid him on the wood, and brought fire. The fire burned him, and the smoke went up to the sky. His wife cried out, and the dog cried out. Then they covered him with earth. They set up a stone above him, and gave libated mead to the dead man. The sun sank. Then night came, and the dog lay down by the stone.

pie: swésōr h₂ḱméni sédyet. h₁ésyeh₂s bʰréh₂tēr h₁ludʰét h₁ésmey-kʷe mléwHt. ph₂tḗr nos mr̥twós h₁ésti. nu kʷís gʷṓs péh₂sti? wéwket. h₁íns h₂léksoh₂. kʷís nos méh₂term̥ h₂életi? h₁íh₂m̥ h₂éloh₂. nu sékʷt. kʷíd swésor dʰédʰeh₁esi? h₂éǵt. péh₂wr̥ h₂léksōh₂ h₁ésyo-kʷe wékʷesh₂ meménoh₂. nu ḱwṓ gʷémt h₁entér-kʷe légʰt.
english: The sister sat by the stone. Her brother arrived, and she said to him: "Our father is dead. Who guards the cattle now?" He said: "I guard them. Who nourishes our mother?" "I nourish her." Then he said: "Sister, what will you do?" She said: "I shall keep the fire, and I shall remember his words." Then the dog came, and lay down between them.

pie: méǵh₂s táwros h₂éǵmn̥ wédʰet sénos-kʷe táwros h₁íh₁ h₁éyt. méǵh₂s táwros h₁ésmey wérh₁yet. sénos h₁ési. n̥sméd h₂epó gʷh₂dʰí. h₂epó gʷéh₂t. sóh₂wl̥ dʰégʷʰet déh₂nu-kʷe térst. h₂éǵmn̥ tr̥syét. méǵh₂s táwros wódr̥ ne widét. h₂élyos h₂ḱméni stéh₂t. sékʷt. wódr̥ wóydh₂e. h₁íd h₂ḱméni Hn̥dʰí h₁ésti. h₁íns h₁íd wédʰet ph₃ént-kʷe tr̥pént-kʷe. h₂nḗr m̥ǵh₂éy táwrōy h₁ésti sénos táwros stóygʰom wóyde.
english: A great bull led the flock, and an old bull went with him. The great bull said to him: "You are old. Go away from us." He went away. The sun was burning, and the river dried up. The flock was thirsty. The great bull did not find water. The other stood by the stone. He said: "I know the water. It is under the stone." He led them to it, and they drank, and they were sated. The great bull has force; the old bull knows the path.

pie: ǵérh₂onts sédyet. snígʷʰs tinéh₁t déh₂nu-kʷe pl̥nh₁tó. snusós h₁ím gʷémt wérh₁t-kʷe. swéḱure moy suHnús ǵeǵónh₁e. ǵérh₂onts h₁ím spéḱyet méwdt-kʷe sékʷt-kʷe. sénos h₁ésmi méroh₂-kʷe méne h₁nómn̥ ne méreti. méne n̥ptéy méne h₁nómn̥ dʰéh₁m̥ h₁éy h₁íd pró bʰérēti. mórtōs m̥rént ḱlutóm h₁nómn̥ gʷíh₃weti.
english: An old man was sitting. The snow was melting, and the river was filling. His daughter-in-law came to him and said: "Father-in-law, a son is born to me." The old man looked at him, and he was glad and said: "I am old, and I shall die; my name shall not die. I set my name on my grandson; he shall carry it forward. Mortals die; a famous name lives."

pie: pótey h₂epó lelóykʷth₂e. kʷís h₂ówins péh₂seti kʷís h₂érh₃yēti? nu h₁widʰéwh₂ h₁ésmi méne ḱḗr stéwdt. h₁n̥gʷnís dʰégʷʰeti h₁ésmi-ge ne sédyesi. téwe sth₂dʰlóm spéḱyoh₂ kúdʰe h₁ési? stóygʰom spéḱyoh₂ wíHre h₂ew gʷm̥dʰí. téwe ǵónh₁ōs HrudHénti. ḱwṓ te h₂isḱéti pékʷom toy ne-kʷe h₁édsi. nu te dʰéǵʰōm ḱéleti.
english: Husband, you are gone away! Who will guard the sheep, who will plough? Now I am a widow, my heart has grown cold! The fire burns, but you do not sit by it. I look at your place; where are you? I look at the road, come back, husband! Your offspring cry out. The dog looks for you; I cooked for you, and you do not eat! Now the earth covers you.

pie: ph₂tḗr kʷékʷloy h₂énti stéh₂t h₁ésyo-kʷe dʰugh₂tréy h₂éǵt. dʰúgh₂ter téwe póteys dʰéh₁mn̥ méne déms h₁éysi. téwe swéḱuroybʰos ḱléwse h₁ésyo-kʷe péh₂wr̥ ph₂sdʰí. téwe pótim mē dʰrugʰyés h₁ésyo dayh₂uréy lewbʰéh₂ h₁sdʰí. h₂wĺ̥h₁neh₂m pĺ̥h₂seh₂m moysóm-kʷe h₁áyso. téwe méh₂term̥ memn̥dʰí. téwe ǵónh₁om h₂éle. deywṓs téwe stóygʰom h₃roǵéyoyh₁ent. h₁yód te h₂égʰos gʷm̥yḗti gʷm̥dʰí nos. dʰéh₁mn̥ nos toy stestóh₂e. dʰúgh₂ter h₁idʰí.
english: The father stood before the wagon and spoke to his daughter: "Daughter, you go from my house to the dwelling of your husband. Listen to your father-in-law, and guard his fire. Do not deceive your husband; be dear to his brother. Take the wool, the garment, and the ram. Remember your mother. Nourish your offspring. May the gods make your path straight. If distress comes upon you, come to us. Our dwelling stands for you. Go, daughter!"

pie: h₁yós sénom ph₂térm̥ h₂élēti ǵr̥h₂n̥tés dṓm tósmey h₁éseti. h₁yós sénom ph₂térm̥ linékʷeti h₂ǵméns kʷid tósmey mē h₁ést. h₁yód suHnús wiHrṓy ne h₁éseti h₁ésyo dʰugh₂trés népōts h₂éǵrom h₁áyetor. h₁yód népōts h₁ésmey ne h₁éseti h₁ésyo bʰréh₂tēr h₁ím h₁áyetor. h₁widʰéwh₂ ǵónh₁ōy h₂éǵrom h₂léksetu. h₁ím kʷis ne h₁áyetor.
english: Whoever nourishes an old father, to him shall belong the old man's house. And whoever leaves an old father, let him have nothing of the flock. If a man has no son, the descendant of his daughter shall take the field. If he has no descendant, his brother shall take it. Let the widow guard the field for the offspring. No one shall take it.

pie: ph₂tḗr ḱéyto tréyes-kʷe tóy h₁ésmi sísdont. suHnús bʰéh₂t. kʷésmōy dṓm dédeh₃si? ǵérh₂onts wérh₁t. tósmey h₁ím dédeh₃mi h₁yós me h₂életi. h₂élyos sékʷt. wódr̥ toy bʰéroh₂. gʷṓs toy h₂mélǵmi. ǵérh₂onts tóysōm h₃épos widét médʰyom-kʷe déyḱet. médʰyos mléwHt. démey te ne h₂élom. dṓm toy h₁ésti.
english: The father lay down, and the three sat by him. One son said: "To whom do you give the house?" The old man answered: "I give it to him who nourishes me." Another said: "I bring you water." "I milk the cows for you." The old man saw their work, and pointed out the middle one. The middle one said: "I did not nourish you for the house." "The house is yours."

pie: h₂éwsōs léwkt. póteys dʰugh₂tḗr h₁nédʰt h₁ésyeh₂s-kʷe méh₂tēr HréwdHt h₁íh₂m̥-kʷe h₂wĺ̥h₁neh₂s pĺ̥h₂seh₂h₁ woséyet. pĺ̥h₂seh₂ h₁rudʰéh₁t. h₂néres kʷékʷlōy gʷṓs yéwgt. kʷékʷlos tetḱnés h₃épos h₁ést yugóm-kʷe dʰh₂bʰrósyo h₃épos h₁ést. h₁ésyeh₂s pótis h₁íh₂m̥ h₁ím úd tl̥néh₂t h₁ésyeh₂s-kʷe bʰréh₂tēr h₁íh₂m̥ sékʷeto. sh₂wéns kʷékʷlos ǵʰleynós h₁ést. dʰugh₂tḗr h₂ew spéḱyet h₁ésyeh₂s-kʷe ḱḗr trémt. h₂éḱmonm̥ dóru-kʷe dʰgʷʰh₂ént. h₁ésyeh₂s swéḱurosyo dṓm kʷsépi h₁ludʰónt. swéḱuros h₂énti stéh₂t mléwHt-kʷe. dʰúgh₂ter wiḱdʰí.
english: Dawn grew bright. The master's daughter came forth, and her mother cried out, and clothed her in a garment of wool. The garment was red. The men yoked the cattle to the wagon. The wagon was the work of the carpenter, and the yoke was the work of the smith. Her husband lifted her up onto it, and her brother followed her. The wheel of the sun was bright. The daughter looked back, and her heart trembled. They passed the stone and the tree. At night they arrived at the house of her father-in-law. The father-in-law stood in front and said: "Enter, daughter."

pie: eḱwos wewekur, "ḱludʰe, owei! ḱerd angʰetai widontbʰyos: ǵʰm̥on, potis, wl̥nam owiyōm kʷr̥neti soi gʷʰermom westrom; owibʰyos kʷe wl̥nā ne esti".
english: The horses said: "Listen, sheep, our hearts pain us when we see this: a man, the master, makes the wool of the sheep into a warm garment for himself. And the sheep has no wool."

pie: dwóh₁ bʰréh₂terh₁ ḱóm tḱitā́m. pótnih₂h₁ wódr̥ deh₂n̥wés duktā́m. h₁íh₂sōm póteyes wr̥ǵyónt sóh₂wl̥ dʰégʷʰet. bʰréh₂tr̥s pótnih₂ h₂élyosyo pótn̥yeh₂ey bʰéh₂t. dʰrugʰyés me. wéwket. ne te dʰrugʰyóm. nu wékʷesh₂ pótins drémt. bʰréh₂tēr h₂élyom stunédt kréwh₂s-kʷe mélh₃t. gʷénh₂h₁ HrudHtā́m swéḱuros-kʷe ḱléwt. h₁ludʰét h₁entér-kʷe stéh₂t. l̥h₁tóm. kʷíd dʰh₁tóm? h₂égʰos ḱóymom pl̥néh₁t. sth₂éh₁yetām ní-kʷe spéḱyetām.
english: Two brothers dwelt together. The two wives drew water from the river. Their husbands were at work; the sun was burning. The wife of one brother spoke to the wife of the other: "You have deceived me." She said: "I did not deceive you." Then the words ran to the husbands. One brother struck the other, and blood came forth. The two women cried out, and the father-in-law heard. He came, and stood between the two. "Let go! What have you done?" Distress filled the household. The two stood, and looked down.

pie: h₁yód suHnús wiHrṓy ǵeǵénh₁eti h₁ésyo déh₃reh₂ bʰérontes ḱéywōs h₁ésyo ḱóymom gʷm̥yónti. poh₂imḗn moysóm wédʰeti pékʷtōr gʰostíbʰos h₁ím pékʷeti gʷḗn mélit bʰéreti dʰh₂bʰrós déh₃rom tḗtḱti tétḱō h₁ésmey yugóm démeti h₁esh₂ós h₁éymos médʰu dédeh₃ti píph₃onti-kʷe h₁dénti-kʷe. h₁yós dóh₃r̥ bʰéreti h₁esh₂ós tósmey déh₃nom dédeh₃ti. ḱéywōs polh₁éwes h₁sénti ǵónh₁oh₁-kʷe bʰuHyéti.
english: When a son is born to a man, his friends come to his household carrying gifts. The shepherd leads a ram; the cook cooks it for the guests; the woman brings honey; the smith makes a gift; the carpenter builds a yoke for him; the master gives them mead, and they drink, and they eat. Whoever brings a gift, to him the master gives a gift. Friends are many, and the offspring grows.

pie: bʰréh₂tēr bʰréh₂trey bʰérǵʰs h₁ésti. dʰrugʰyóntih₂ dn̥ǵʰwéh₂s bʰréh₂tern̥s bʰinédti. dn̥ǵʰwéh₂s h₁ógʷʰis h₁ésti. ǵr̥h₂n̥tés wékʷos stóygʰos h₁ésti. méh₂tr̥s ḱḗr h₁n̥gʷnís h₁ésti. h₁wésus swéḱuros ǵʰiméni péh₂wr̥ h₁ésti. h₁uséwih₂ snusós mélit h₁ésti. dusḱléwēs dayh₂wḗr h₂béli kʷŕ̥mis h₁ésti. h₁yéh₂ h₁ésyeh₂s pótim dʰrugʰyéti séh₂ dʰh₁méni wĺ̥kʷos h₁ésti. mélit dʰrugʰyóntey tósmey dn̥ǵʰwéh₂i h₁ésti h₁ógʷʰis-kʷe ḱérdi h₁ésti. wĺ̥kʷos ḱwṓ ne bʰúHt. dwóh₁ bʰréh₂terh₁ kʷékʷlom yugóy duktés. bʰréh₂teres ḱóm kʷór sédyonti h₁n̥gʷnís h₂én dʰégʷʰeti. ḱód sénom wékʷos h₁ésti.
english: A brother is a stronghold for a brother. A deceiving tongue splits brothers. The tongue is a serpent. The word of an old man is a path. The heart of a mother is a fire. A good father-in-law is a fire in winter. A good daughter-in-law is honey. A brother-in-law of ill fame is a worm in the apple. She who deceives her husband is a wolf in the dwelling. For the deceiver there is honey on the tongue, and a serpent in the heart. A wolf does not become a dog. Two brothers draw the wagon under the yoke. Where brothers sit together, there the fire burns. This is the old word.

pie: akwāsas ā wawakant: krudʰi awai, kard agʰnutai wiwidwant- swas: manus patis warnām awisāms karnauti swabʰyam gʰarmam wastram awibʰyams ka warnā na asti.
english: The horses said: "Listen, sheep, our hearts pain us when we see this: a man, the master, makes the wool of the sheep into a warm garment for himself. And the sheep has no wool."

pie: kʷíd mórtos bʰéreti? h₁íd h₁ésyo h₂mési ne h₁ésti. h₁ésyo ph₂tḗr h₁ésmey h₁íd ǵn̥h₁téy dʰéh₁t. mórtōs h₁íd mluHénti. mórtos h₁íd ḱléwseti. h₁íd kʷis ne h₁édti h₁íd kʷis ne píph₃eti. péh₂wr̥ h₁íd ne h₁éwseti wódr̥ h₁íd h₂epó ne wéǵʰeti. h₁yód mórtos dʰǵʰémi ḱéytor h₁íd gʷíh₃weti. kʷíd h₁íd h₁ésti? h₁íd h₁nómn̥ h₁ésti.
english: What does the man carry? It is not on his shoulder. His father set it on him at birth. Men say it. The man listens to it. No one eats it, no one drinks it. Fire does not burn it, water does not carry it away. When the man lies in the earth, it lives. What is it? It is the name.

pie: dwóh₁ bʰréh₂terh₁ ph₂téri sth₂éh₁yetām. tóh₁ ḱléwset nu-kʷe wérh₁yet. h₁yós swóm bʰréh₂term̥ stunédt só h₂élyōy moysóm h₁opéyetu. h₁yéh₂-kʷe dʰrugʰyét séh₂ h₂élyosyo gʷnéh₂ey wódr̥ bʰéretu. nu h₁ésyo wékʷos ḱlutā́m. só moysóm h₁ím wédʰet h₁íh₂-kʷe wódr̥ bʰéret. nu ǵérh₂onts mléwHt. sdtóm wéyh₁onm̥-kʷe píph₃etom. bʰréh₂tr̥s kréwh₂s wódr̥ ne h₁ésti. sísdetām ph₃tā́m-kʷe.
english: The two brothers stood before the father. He listened to the two, and then he said: "Whoever struck his own brother, let that man give a ram to the other. And she who deceived, let her bring water to the woman of the other." The two heard his word. That man led a ram to him, and she brought water. Then the old man said: "Sit down, and drink the wine. The blood of a brother is not water." The two sat down, and drank.

pie: h₁regʷesyét. kʷséps stéwdt. poh₂imnés pótnih₂ démi légʰyet h₁ésyeh₂s-kʷe pótis bʰéwdʰet. nu h₂éwsōs léwkt dyḗws-kʷe h₁rudʰéh₁t mélh₃t-kʷe suHnús. HréwdHt. nu ph₂tḗr h₁ím widét swóm-kʷe ḱḗr méwdt. nu ph₂tḗr h₁ím sóh₂wl̥ woydéyet h₁ésmey-kʷe ḱlutóm h₁nómn̥ dʰéh₁t wérh₁yet-kʷe. polh₁úh₂ wétesh₂ gʷíh₃woyh₁s téwe h₁nómn̥ mē mr̥yéh₁t ń̥dʰgʷʰitom toy ḱléwos h₁syéh₁t. nu méh₂tēr h₁ím ḱléwt h₂éǵt-kʷe. h₁éy nos lewbʰós h₁ésti h₂uksyéh₁t Hwr̥dʰyéh₁t-kʷe.
english: It was growing dark. The night grew cold. The shepherd's wife lay in the house and her husband was awake. Then the dawn grew bright and the sky was red, and a son came forth. He cried out. Then the father saw him and his own heart grew joyful. Then the father showed him the sun, and set a famous name on him, and said: "May you live many years; may your name not die; may imperishable fame be yours!" The mother heard him and said: "Dear is he to us; may he grow up, and may he be strong!"

pie: ph₂ter stóygʰoh₁ h₁idʰí ph₂trṓm stóygʰoh₁ h₁idʰí. déh₂nu nh₂éwh₁ gʷh₂dʰí néh₂us h₁ím wéǵʰoyh₁t. h₂éwsos diwés dʰúgh₂ter h₁ésmey lukdʰí. sóh₂wl̥ h₁ím spéḱye dʰéǵʰom méh₂ter h₁ím h₁áyso. ph₂tr̥bʰís sdyéh₁t ǵʰutóm médʰu ph₃yéh₁t. h₁ésyo h₁nómn̥ mē mr̥yéh₁t. h₁ésyo ḱléwos ń̥dʰgʷʰitom h₁syéh₁t h₁ím memn̥mé.
english: Go, father, by the path, go by the path of the fathers! Cross the river in the boat, may the boat carry him! Dawn, daughter of Sky, grow bright for him! Sun, look upon him, Mother Earth, receive him! May he sit with the fathers, may he drink the libated mead! May his name not die! May his fame be imperishable, we remember him.

pie: h₂nḗr pótis-kʷe sdtā́m. pótis wérh₁yet. méne toy dʰugh₂térm̥ dédeh₃mi. téwe moy bʰoydʰéh₂m dh₃dʰí. bʰoydʰā́s dh₃tā́m. nu h₂nḗr sékʷt. dyḗws ḱléwseti dʰéǵʰōm-kʷe méh₂tēr ḱléwseti. sóh₂wl̥ h₁íh₂m̥ dedórḱe déh₂nu-kʷe h₁íh₂m̥ ǵn̥néh₃ti. h₁yós ḱā́m bʰoydʰéh₂m Hrunépeti h₁ésyo gʷówes n̥ḱih₁ént h₁ésyo h₁nómn̥ mr̥yéh₁t. nu wéyh₁onm̥ ph₃tā́m kʷséps-kʷe gʷémt.
english: The man and the master sat down. The master said: "I give you my daughter. Give me your pledge." The two gave their pledges. Then the man said: "The sky hears, and Mother Earth hears. The sun has seen it, and the river knows it. Whoever breaks this pledge, may his cattle vanish, may his name die!" Then the two drank wine, and night came.

pie: gʷḗn h₁ésyeh₂s pótim kʷsépi gʷémt wérh₁t-kʷe. ḱludʰí me. téwe moy bʰréh₂tēr wéwket. sékʷt. démi nos gʰóstis h₁ési. mélit nos nos h₃éngʷn̥-kʷe h₁édsi. gʰóstis ne h₁ésmi téwe pótnih₂ h₁ésmi. h₁íh₂m̥ ḱléwset wérh₁yet-kʷe. ḱód wéwket? h₁íd wéwket. méne bʰréh₂term̥ h₁r̥sḱṓh₂ h₁ésmey-kʷe bʰéh₂oh₂. ḱósmi ḱóymoy gʰóstis ne h₁ési lewbʰéh₂ moy h₁ési. nu stéh₂t h₁ím-kʷe gʷéh₂t. h₁ím h₁éḱwōys widét h₁ésmey-kʷe bʰéh₂t.
english: At night the woman came to her husband and said: "Hear me. Your brother has spoken to me. He said: 'You are a stranger in our house. You eat our honey and our butter.' I am not a stranger; I am your wife." He listened to her, and said: "Did he say this?" "He said it." "I shall go to my brother, and I shall speak to him. You are not a stranger in this household; you are dear to me." Then he rose, and went to him. He found him with the horses, and spoke to him.
